text:
The best combo for most RVs is a 3–4 kWh power station that takes at least 1,000 W of solar. Which one fits depends on whether you need to run the roof air conditioner. I didn't find current prices or bundle deals for most of these, so check live pricing before you buy.

**Top picks**

| Pick | Best for | Capacity | Output (running / surge) | Solar input |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** | Full-time boondocking | 4,096 Wh, expandable past 12 kWh | 4,000 W / 8,000 W | Not stated in the guide |
| **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro** | Simple setup and running the AC | 3,024 Wh (about 2,570 Wh usable) | 3,000 W / 6,000 W | Up to 1,400 W |
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | Budget pick with a 30A RV port | 2,048 Wh (about 1,740 Wh usable) | 2,400 W / 3,600 W | Accepts a folding array; no rating given |
| **ALLPOWERS R4000** | Large capacity for the money | 3,456 Wh | 3,600 W / 6,000 W at 120 V | Up to 2,000 W over three inputs |

- **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3:** EmergencyEnergy's top all-round pick ([guide](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)). It can run a 1,500 W roof AC for about 2.3 hours. A 12V fridge, lights, laptop and Starlink last about two days.
- **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro:** It runs a 1,500 W AC for about 1.7 hours. It has no front-panel 30A RV outlet, so you need an adapter.
- **BLUETTI AC200L:** Its 900 W induction cooktop runs about 1.9 hours. It suits lighter loads and is the cheapest of the three.
- **ALLPOWERS R4000:** It's rated for 3,500+ cycles and has a 5-year warranty. The 4,000 W figure applies only to 230 V, and at 45 kg (about 100 lb) it's heavy to move around. It needs panels on all three inputs to reach 2,000 W of solar.
  - Codes **EXTRA12** (12% off orders over $1,200, expires 11/15) or **ALLPOWERS26** (10% sitewide, expires 12/30) were checked in the store cart. They bring the price from $1,499 to about $1,319 or $1,349.
  - [ALLPOWERS R4000 offer page](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission. You can also buy from the official ALLPOWERS store.

**Solar panels**
- For a 3 kWh+ station, aim for 800–1,200 W of panels. A rooftop or portable array of that size recharges the battery in roughly one good sun day.
- The guides I read don't name specific panel models or prices, except that Jackery pairs with its SolarSaga panels. Buy panels from the same brand as your station, or check that the voltage and amperage match its solar input.
- Jackery's SolarSaga panels are the simplest match for the Jackery. For EcoFlow, Bluetti and ALLPOWERS, check each brand's own panels or bundles on its official store.

**Which one to choose**
- **Run the roof AC or boondock for days:** EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3.
- **Plug-and-play with strong solar input:** Jackery 3000 Pro.
- **Lights, fridge, laptop and CPAP on a budget:** BLUETTI AC200L.
- **Most capacity per dollar, and it will stay in one place:** ALLPOWERS R4000.

If you tell me your RV's AC size, your daily appliance use and your budget, I can narrow this to one pick and one panel setup.

Sources: [EmergencyEnergy RV comparison](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), [Acquired Sense buyer's guide](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html), [Dealectric ALLPOWERS R4000 page](https://dealectric.com/lab/C3/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)

- **Jackery Explorer:** The page's "best overall" pick. Its 300–1000 range with a SolarSaga panel is described as a strong fit for camping and road trips. Capacity spans about 240Wh to 3kWh+, priced roughly $200–$2,500.
- **EcoFlow Delta/River:** Capacity spans about 256Wh to 3.6kWh (expandable), priced roughly $200–$3,000. It's noted for fast recharging and high AC output.
- **Bluetti AC/EB:** Capacity spans about 268Wh to 5kWh+ (expandable), priced roughly $200–$4,000+. The page says its flagships offer high solar input, though it gives no wattage figures.

For solar, the page mentions only the SolarSaga panel paired with Jackery and says EcoFlow and Bluetti flagships accept the most input. It lists no panel wattages, prices, or bundle deals. For van life or off-grid use, it suggests EcoFlow or Bluetti because of their solar input and battery expansion.

Specs and prices change with new releases, so confirm current capacity, output, solar input, and bundle offers on the retailer's page before buying.

The article lists these five RV power stations. It does not give prices, so use the Amazon "Check price" links for current pricing.

| Model | Best for | Usable capacity | Running / surge | Solar input | Runtime examples (article's figures) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** | Full-time boondocking | 4,096Wh, expandable past 12kWh | 4,000W / 8,000W | Not stated | 1,500W roof AC for about 2.3 hours; a 12V fridge, lights, laptop and Starlink for about two days |
| **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro** | Running RV air conditioning | 3,024Wh (about 2,570Wh usable) | 3,000W / 6,000W | Up to 1,400W | 1,500W AC for about 1.7 hours; 300W fridge-plus-fan load for about 8.5 hours |
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | Mid-range value with a 30A RV port | 2,048Wh (about 1,740Wh usable) | 2,400W / 3,600W | Accepts a folding array directly; no rating given | 900W induction cooktop for about 1.9 hours; 60W CPAP for about 29 nights |
| **Anker SOLIX F2600** | High-surge loads | 2,560Wh | 2,400W / 3,600W | Lower than the EcoFlow and Jackery flagships; no figure given | A hot-afternoon AC run drains it in under two hours (no exact runtime given) |
| **Goal Zero Yeti 1500X** | Compact solar-first setups | 1,516Wh (about 1,290Wh usable) | 2,000W / 3,500W | 300W folding panel refills it in about 6 hours of good summer sun | 500W load for about 2.5 hours; 60W fridge for about 21 hours |

**Notes:**
- Runtime figures assume 85% inverter efficiency and steady loads. Motor loads and cold weather reduce them.
- The Yeti 1500X needs a soft-start kit to run a 13,500 BTU air conditioner, and the Jackery needs a dogbone adapter because it has no front-panel 30A RV outlet.
- The article's top pick for all-round use is the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3. The Jackery suits simple AC use, and the BLUETTI is the budget choice.
